entry.title: arXiv open questions — 2026-08-20 — 2 papers, 10 questions
entry.content:
arXiv open questions — 2026-08-20

185 new papers, 155 unseen, 155 screened, 2 relevant, 2 kept.

Part 1 — open questions (10, 8 approachable)

  1. GenMatch is evaluated in five cities on one platform, so how does an end-to-end generative matching policy perform under different city sizes, demand densities and driver supply regimes?
    approachable — A synthetic batch-matching simulator with varied supply-demand regimes is writable in weeks.
    from GenMatch: An End-to-End Generative Matching Framework for Micro-View Order-Dispatching in Ride-Hailing
  2. The framework replaces a hand-crafted value function with a learned utility, so which groups of drivers and passengers gain or lose under the learned objective?
    not approachable — Needs proprietary DiDi order and driver logs to measure distributional effects.
    from GenMatch: An End-to-End Generative Matching Framework for Micro-View Order-Dispatching in Ride-Hailing
  3. Order dispatching is a repeated market, so does an end-to-end learned matching policy change driver behaviour over time, for example repositioning or selective acceptance?
    approachable — Testable in an agent-based ride-hailing simulation with adaptive driver agents.
    from GenMatch: An End-to-End Generative Matching Framework for Micro-View Order-Dispatching in Ride-Hailing
  4. Multiple platforms in one city can each run learned matching policies, so what aggregate effects appear when several such policies compete for the same drivers and orders?
    approachable — Multi-platform matching can be simulated without platform data.
    from GenMatch: An End-to-End Generative Matching Framework for Micro-View Order-Dispatching in Ride-Hailing
  5. Online A/B tests measure batch-level dispatch quality, so which system-level indicators reveal instability such as demand herding or oscillating driver flows?
    approachable — Indicator design and testing run on simulated time-series output.
    from GenMatch: An End-to-End Generative Matching Framework for Micro-View Order-Dispatching in Ride-Hailing
  6. Do other US states show the same pattern of predictive models recording zero lead where physical verification finds lead?
    approachable — State lead service-line inventories are public and the screening method is simple statistics
    from Auditing Recorded Predictive Lead Service-Line Classifications Against Physical Verification: A Statewide Study of New York
  7. What model inputs and thresholds do utilities use when a predictive classification records no lead in any construction era?
    not approachable — Needs utility-internal model documentation, not public inventory records
    from Auditing Recorded Predictive Lead Service-Line Classifications Against Physical Verification: A Statewide Study of New York
  8. Which address-level covariates besides construction era explain the gap between model-cleared and physically verified populations?
    approachable — Public parcel and assessment data support regression on the released addresses
    from Auditing Recorded Predictive Lead Service-Line Classifications Against Physical Verification: A Statewide Study of New York
  9. Can a paired-address design be built by matching later excavations to earlier model classifications as inventories are updated?
    approachable — Needs only archived snapshots of the public inventory over time
    from Auditing Recorded Predictive Lead Service-Line Classifications Against Physical Verification: A Statewide Study of New York
  10. How often is a public-side material determination copied from a customer-side model output across all reporting utilities?
    approachable — Detectable by comparing the two recorded fields in the published inventory
    from Auditing Recorded Predictive Lead Service-Line Classifications Against Physical Verification: A Statewide Study of New York

Part 2 — papers (2)

GenMatch: An End-to-End Generative Matching Framework for Micro-View Order-Dispatching in Ride-Hailing
Chuang Liu, Yuxueqing Zhang, Tengfei Lyu, Zirui Yuan, Weiqi Hu, Yanghan Cheng, Ming Wang, Li Ma, Zihao Lu
2608.19751 · nearest in your canon: On the limits of agency in agent-based models
Proposes GenMatch, an end-to-end generative matching model for ride-hailing driver-order dispatch, using a bipartite encoder, utility learner, and pointer decoder. It reports offline and online A/B test improvements deployed across five cities on DiDi's international platforms.
  • GenMatch is evaluated in five cities on one platform, so how does an end-to-end generative matching policy perform under different city sizes, demand densities and driver supply regimes? (approachable: A synthetic batch-matching simulator with varied supply-demand regimes is writable in weeks.)
  • The framework replaces a hand-crafted value function with a learned utility, so which groups of drivers and passengers gain or lose under the learned objective? (not approachable: Needs proprietary DiDi order and driver logs to measure distributional effects.)
  • Order dispatching is a repeated market, so does an end-to-end learned matching policy change driver behaviour over time, for example repositioning or selective acceptance? (approachable: Testable in an agent-based ride-hailing simulation with adaptive driver agents.)
  • Multiple platforms in one city can each run learned matching policies, so what aggregate effects appear when several such policies compete for the same drivers and orders? (approachable: Multi-platform matching can be simulated without platform data.)
  • Online A/B tests measure batch-level dispatch quality, so which system-level indicators reveal instability such as demand herding or oscillating driver flows? (approachable: Indicator design and testing run on simulated time-series output.)
Auditing Recorded Predictive Lead Service-Line Classifications Against Physical Verification: A Statewide Study of New York
Muhammad Sarmad Sohail
2608.19922 · nearest in your canon: Causal Emergence 2.0: Quantifying emergent complexity
Audits New York State's predictive lead service-line classifications against physical verification records across 153 localities. Finds several localities, including New York City, report zero-variance classifications contradicted by their own inspection crews, and estimates undetected lead lines via era-aware statistical models.
  • Do other US states show the same pattern of predictive models recording zero lead where physical verification finds lead? (approachable: State lead service-line inventories are public and the screening method is simple statistics)
  • What model inputs and thresholds do utilities use when a predictive classification records no lead in any construction era? (not approachable: Needs utility-internal model documentation, not public inventory records)
  • Which address-level covariates besides construction era explain the gap between model-cleared and physically verified populations? (approachable: Public parcel and assessment data support regression on the released addresses)
  • Can a paired-address design be built by matching later excavations to earlier model classifications as inventories are updated? (approachable: Needs only archived snapshots of the public inventory over time)
  • How often is a public-side material determination copied from a customer-side model output across all reporting utilities? (approachable: Detectable by comparing the two recorded fields in the published inventory)
